system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, no language over the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, the encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

For every objection also fill `uae_basis`: if one of the UAE clauses shown (ids starting with ITU-UAE:, TDRA-,
UAE-, DXB-) speaks to this issue, set status "cites_uae" with its id and a word-for-word quote; otherwise set
status "none_applies" with empty ref and quote. Say "none_applies" honestly: it tells the regulator where UAE
texts are silent.

[TS23041#0043] 3GPP TS 23.041 Technical realization of Cell Broadcast Service (CBS), version 18.3.0 Release 18 (ETSI TS 123 041 V18.3.0) (p.11):
2 General description The CBS service is analogous to the Teletex service offered on television, in that like Teletex, it permits a number of unacknowledged general CBS messages to be broadcast to all receivers within a particular region. CBS messages are broadcast to defined geographical areas known as cell broadcast areas. These areas may comprise of one or more cells, or may comprise the entire PLMN or SNPN. Individual CBS messages will be assigned their own geographical coverage areas by mutual agreement between the information provider and the PLMN or SNPN operator. CBS messages may originate from a number of Cell Broadcast Entities (CBEs), which are connected to the Cell Broadcast Centre. CBS messages are then sent from the CBC to the cells, in accordance with the CBS's coverage requirements. A CBS page comprises of 82 octets, which, using the default character set, equates to 93 characters. Other Data Coding Schemes may also be used, as described in 3GPP TS 23.038 [3]. Up to 15 of these pages may be concatenated to form a CBS messagee. Each page of such CBS message will have the same message identifier (indicating the source of the message), and the same serial number. Using this information, the MS/UE is able to identify and ignore re-broadcasts of already received messages.

9.3.19.1 Identification of a directory number within a CBS-Message-Information-Page For information relating to this feature see 3GPP TS 23.040 [4]. 9.3.20 CBS-Message-Information-Length n This parameter gives the number of octets of the CBS-Message-Information-Page n containing user information. The remaining octets of the CBS-Message-Information-Page n contain only padding information and are not included in this parameter. In the case where the user information is encoded using the GSM 7 bit default alphabet and the last character terminates at an octet boundary, this parameter indicates the number of octets of user information. In the case where the last character does not terminate at an octet boundary, this parameter indicates the number of octets up to the octet boundary immediately following the last GSM 7 bit default alphabet character of user information. In UMTS and E-UTRAN, the CBS-Message-Information-Pages together with the associated CBS-MessageInformation-Length parameter are broadcasted as a single unit over the radio inteface, and are part of 'CB Data' parameter at the UE.

data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. English is GSM-7 at 3 pages and Arabic is UCS-2 at 7 pages, both well under the 15-page maximum. Page count beyond that is a recorded gap (G6), so I do not object to it. The text carries no protective action, and the Arabic first page (about 41 characters) cuts off after 'winds' before naming the dust and sand hazard. No clause shown covers either point, so I record them as no-basis concerns for the approvers.

no_basis.concern: The phone text gives no protective action for the public, only the hazard, visibility and time window. The first page of each language therefore carries no action.
no_basis.searched_for: clause requiring the hazard and the recommended action on the first cell broadcast page

no_basis.concern: The Arabic first page holds only about 41 characters, so it ends after 'من رياح' (of winds). The dust and sand hazard and the visibility reduction fall on later pages.
